audit_meta.scope: Full codebase — static analysis only (backend/frontend services offline)

findings.title: Vitest UI Server Arbitrary File Read / Remote Code Execution
findings.exploit_scenario: Any network peer that can reach the Vitest UI dev server can read arbitrary filesystem paths (e.g. .env, source maps) and execute code without credentials.
findings.impact: Credential theft, source exfiltration, CI environment compromise.

findings.title: Handlebars.js JavaScript Injection via AST Type Confusion (Multiple CVEs)
findings.exploit_scenario: If any code path compiles a Handlebars template supplied by an untrusted source, an attacker can achieve arbitrary JavaScript execution via AST type confusion.
findings.impact: Remote code execution if user-supplied templates are ever processed.
findings.recommendation: Run npm ls handlebars to identify root dependency; npm audit fix to patch. Verify no user input reaches template compilation.
findings.timeline: IMMEDIATE — audit the chain today, patch before next sprint

findings.title: Traceability Enforcer Covers Only 12% of Canonical Specifications
findings.exploit_scenario: A regression in portal/ or platform/ code (88% of FRs) passes all CI verification gates undetected.
findings.impact: Silent spec drift; broken features ship without failing any gate.
findings.recommendation:
Add --multi mode or per-spec CI invocations:
  python3 tools/traceability-enforcer.py --file Specifications/dev-workflow-platform.md --source portal/
  python3 tools/traceability-enforcer.py --file Specifications/tiered-merge-pipeline.md --source platform/

findings.title: FR-073 through FR-095 Referenced in Code but Defined in No Specification
findings.exploit_scenario: 23 phantom requirement IDs are verified in code comments but do not exist in any spec document. Anyone reading Specifications/ as the source of truth will miss these features entirely.
findings.impact: Spec integrity violation; future changes to image upload/orchestrator proxy lack a requirements baseline.
findings.recommendation: Add FR-073–FR-095 to Specifications/dev-workflow-platform.md with acceptance criteria, or create Specifications/image-upload.md.

findings.title: Vite server.fs.deny Bypass via Windows Alternate Paths
findings.exploit_scenario: On Windows development environments, server.fs.deny rules can be bypassed using short names or UNC paths, serving protected files.
findings.impact: Developer credential/config file exposure on Windows machines.

findings.title: Vite Path Traversal in .map File Handling
findings.exploit_scenario: Crafted .map file requests can traverse directories outside the intended scope in both dev and build scenarios.
findings.impact: Arbitrary file read from dev server.
findings.recommendation: Upgrade vite to ^6.4.3 (addresses both DEP-003 and DEP-004)

findings.title: form-data CRLF Injection in Multipart Field Names
findings.exploit_scenario: Unescaped multipart field names/filenames allow CRLF injection — attacker can split HTTP responses or inject headers in multipart requests.
findings.impact: HTTP header injection, response splitting in file upload flows.
findings.recommendation: npm install form-data@^4.0.6 (or npm audit fix)

findings.title: ws WebSocket Library Memory Exhaustion DoS via Tiny Fragments
findings.file: Source/Frontend (transitive via Vite or test framework)
findings.exploit_scenario: Attacker sends many tiny WebSocket fragments, exhausting server memory and causing DoS for all connected clients.
findings.impact: Process/server crash if WebSocket connections are exposed.
findings.recommendation: npm install ws@^8.21.0 (or via Vite upgrade)
